contract_evolution_review.rationale: v0.4.2 produced the second avoidable late release escape in the train. Although earlier repairs moved PR-candidate provider/runtime/UI evidence before merge, the release architecture still treated the protected tag as the trigger for first execution of several deterministic release blockers. The v0.4.2 Release workflow failed before its Codex Draft runtime because an Actions GITHUB_TOKEN could not verify the repository immutable-release setting. The full audit therefore repairs the class, not the symptom: PRETAG_BLOCKER_CLOSURE makes accepted-main exact-byte staging the latest allowed boundary for reproducible blockers; provider latest/integrity is frozen in stage evidence; repository-admin policy is checked by the Owner-authenticated boundary; full CI no longer reruns on tag; tag automation only binds/promotes/reconciles already accepted bytes; and transient transport failures on unchanged bytes are retryable on the same protected tag rather than consuming another version.
